claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To get started, could you please tell me how many children you're looking to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! I'm looking to claim for my son Alex. He's my only child.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! I'll need to ask a few questions about Alex to determine your eligibility.

How old is Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's 8 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you. And could you tell me, do you live in the United Kingdom (England, Scotland, Wales, or Northern Ireland)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in England - in Leeds actually.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you. Now I need to ask a few more questions about your situation with Alex.

Is Alex living with you?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he doesn't live with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know. Since Alex doesn't live with you, could you tell me a bit more about his living situation?

Are you contributing financially towards Alex's upbringing (for example, paying at least the same amount as the current Child Benefit rate towards his care, food, clothing, etc.)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I do help out financially. I contribute towards his clothes, school things, and help with his activities and such.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for that information. Just to clarify, do you contribute at least £26.05 per week (or an equivalent amount) towards Alex's upkeep? This is the current Child Benefit rate for a first child.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's right - I pay £26.05 a week towards his upkeep.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. A couple more questions about your circumstances:

Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. And one more question:

Does Alex live with his other parent, a guardian, or someone else? And is there a reason why only you are claiming rather than the person Alex lives with?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He lives with his mum, but she's not claiming Child Benefit for him. I'm the one who contributes financially to his upkeep, so I'm looking to claim it.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for explaining that. Just one more question to confirm:

Are you currently working or receiving benefits in another country (outside the UK), or is the other parent working or receiving benefits in another country? This can sometimes affect Child Benefit eligibility.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, neither of us is working or receiving benefits in another country. We're both based here in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for providing all that information. I now have everything I need to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided, I'm pleased to tell you that **you appear to be eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's a summary of why:

**For Alex:**
- ✅ He is 8 years old, which is under 16 (meets the age requirement)
- ✅ Although Alex doesn't live with you, you are contributing at least £26.05 per week towards his upkeep, which equals or exceeds the Child Benefit rate
- ✅ No one else is currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex
- ✅ You live in the UK
- ✅ Neither you nor Alex's mother is working or receiving benefits from another country

You can claim Child Benefit even if your child doesn't live with you, as long as you're contributing towards their upkeep at a rate at least equal to the Child Benefit amount – which you are.

To make your claim, you'll need to complete a Child Benefit claim form. You can do this online through the official government website or by post.

Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit?
